record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.original_question: How can the ant-inspired reinforcement model be extended to transient graphs such as Z^d or regular trees, for example by introducing a density of food sources, adding a weak drift toward the origin, or conditioning walks to hit the set of food sources, and what limiting reinforced structure results in those transient settings?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Extend the model to transient graphs, such as Z d or regular trees. This could be done by putting a density of sources of food or by considering a walks with a (weak) drift towards the origin, or conditioned to hit the set of sources of food.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following ant-inspired reinforcement model. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a locally finite connected graph with a distinguished vertex $o\in V$ ("origin"/nest) and a designated nonempty set $F\subset V$ of "food sources." A walker performs a discrete-time nearest-neighbor random walk on $G$ starting at $o$. Each directed edge $e$ carries a weight $w_n(e)\ge 0$ that is updated at each step: when the walker traverses a directed edge $e$, its weight is reinforced (for instance multiplicatively, $w_{n+1}(e)=w_n(e)+1$, or exponentially), and the walker's next step from its current vertex $v$ is chosen among the outgoing directed edges from $v$ with probability proportional to their current weights. Successive walkers ("ants") are launched from $o$ in this reinforced environment, possibly removing the source upon reaching $F$ and restarting from $o$.

On recurrent base graphs such as $\mathbb{Z}$ or finite graphs this defines a well-studied "ant random walk," and one can ask about the long-time geometry of the reinforced edge weights and the trails connecting $o$ to $F$.

Problem. Formulate and analyze a meaningful extension of this ant-inspired reinforcement model to transient base graphs, in particular:
(a) the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d\ge 3$, and
(b) infinite regular trees $\mathbb{T}_k$ with $k\ge 3$.

Possible modifications to obtain a non-degenerate model include:
(i) replacing the single source by a random (e.g.\ Bernoulli or Poisson) density of food sources in $V$;
(ii) biasing each walker by a weak drift toward the origin $o$ (for instance multiplying transition weights by $e^{-\lambda\,d(v',o)+\lambda\,d(v,o)}$ for a small parameter $\lambda>0$);
(iii) conditioning each walker's trajectory on hitting the set of food sources in finite time.

Determine, for at least one such formulation: (1) whether the sequence of trajectories is almost surely well-defined and returns to $o$; (2) the asymptotic behavior of the reinforced edge-weight field as the number of ants tends to infinity; and (3) whether a limiting reinforced structure (e.g.\ a random tree, a finite collection of trails, or a stationary edge-weight measure) emerges connecting $o$ to the food sources, and describe it.
artifact.status_search_result: The ant-inspired (directed edge) reinforced random walk has been analyzed on $\mathbb{Z}$ (escapes to infinity with a law of large numbers) and on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge 2$, and finite non-tree graphs (almost sure trapping in a directed circuit — "ant mill"). No published work appears to address the proposed extensions to transient graphs with a density of food sources, a weak drift toward the origin, or conditioning on hitting food sources, and no limiting reinforced structure in those settings has been identified. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Directed Edge Reinforced Random Walk: The Ant Mill Phenomenon
status_evidence.snippet: On non-tree finite graphs and on Z^d with d>=2, the Ant RW almost surely gets eventually trapped into some directed circuit. In Z, the Ant RW escapes to infinity and satisfies a LLN with random limit.
status_evidence.claim: Behavior known on Z and Z^d (d>=2) without food-source/drift modifications; transient-graph extensions with food sources are not treated.

status_evidence.title: Walk this way: modeling foraging ant dynamics in multiple food source environments
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice foraging model with pheromone reinforcement; ants converge to a trail connecting nest to food source after a transient Gaussian phase.
status_evidence.claim: Simulation-style models exist on lattices but rigorous limiting reinforced structures on transient graphs Z^d or trees remain unresolved.
